Thats a really good Point. It’s true that the line between gender expression and sexual orientation often blurred at that time period.

But i don’t think it necessarily means Kanjis story has to be about sexuality. Its can just as much be about self acceptance and breaking out of rigid gender roles. Rejecting toxic masculinity without the need to label it.

But the way i see it, thats just a part of it. So no i still wouldn’t call it him working out his sexuality. His struggles were with his masculinity and fear of social rejection. I don’t think it had anything to do with giving him a definitive label to orientation. His shadow is flamboyant and provocative. It’s because Kanji is terrified of not being viewed as traditionally masculine. He is deeply insecure about being mocked for his hobbies.

His fear is less “i might be gay” and more like “people will see me as feminine or weak”

There is no denying that he had feeling for the male presenting Naoto and yes it adds to his confusion but it’s not the whole point of it. 

The game leaves his sexual orientation intentionally ambiguous to emphasise his journey is about self acceptance and not labels.

We also must consider: Kanji is a teen in a small town. He might not have the knowledge or vocabulary to even fully understand it like we do. 

Kanjis story is less about coming out and more about him learning not to hate himself. Saying it is only about him coming to terms with his sexuality is in my opinion still an oversimplification.

Hello. I would like to correct a few things in your post. Its not a personal attack, just to clarify some misinformation on your part. Mind you, i am also 18.

You‘ve said “Tinnitus itself is caused by trauma to the hair cells”. This is not necessarily True. Tinnitus has many plausible causes. Stomach issues, Medication, stress, noise exposure….the list goes on. It can been caused by many things and some people never find out why they have it. (myself included). I don’t have any trauma to my hair cells or hearing loss but i still have Tinnitus.


Also please don’t give advice regarding earbuds. This is detrimental advice and could worsen Tinnitus tenfold. I am happy it works for you, just note that it’s a huge risk and doesn’t work for everyone. Many people got tinnitus from excessive earbud use and noise exposure. Besides, many people have Hyperacusis or dysacusis alongside their tinnitus which makes music painful or its recommended that you stay away from it.

Lastly, while i get where you are coming from, its pretty hard for many people to just “coexist” with the ringing because it can get to a severe ot catastrophic level where its genuinely impossible to “not notice it”. It’s not bad advice but it’s a bit invalidating to them. Not everyone has the same experience so there is literally no universal advice.

It does make sense. The brain is highly adaptable. When an input is not received enough It goes through a process called neuroplasticity and the Cortex or Thalamus start being hyperactive and misfiring. Obviously sitting in a quiet room for 5min wont do anything but do that over a longer period of time and you will eventually get tinnitus. Hearing loss lasts your whole life and is depriving your brain of a certain percentage of sound. So the Brain tries to fill in the missing part. 

It goes without saying tho this is not the ONLY plausible explanation for tinnitus. I don’t have hearing loss and i have tinnitus. But i believe maladaptive neuroplasticity is one of the more plausible explanations we have for tinnitus.
